title: multi-region-routing-rule-authoring-and-validation-playbook
content:
Purpose:
Provide an opinionated authoring guide, canonical JSON/YAML schema examples, validation rules, and progressive rollout mechanics for multi-region routing rules used by the control plane. This doc is a working playbook: authoritative for the platform-engineering team but intended to be readable by SREs, solutions engineers, and product owners who author traffic policies.

Audience and scope:
- Authors of routing rule config (PRs, UI policy editors)
- Validators and linting engineers integrating checks into CI
- Release engineers automating canary rollouts and rollback flows

Principles:
- Small, composable rules: prefer many narrow rules over one monolithic rule set.
- Deterministic evaluation: rules must include explicit priority/ordering and deterministic tie-breakers.
- Fail-safe defaults: any unmatched request uses a well-defined fallback (global-default).
- Observable changes: each rule change must be associated with a rollout marker and metric tags.

Canonical schema (human-friendly outline):
- id: string (stable, immutable after release)
- description: string
- priority: integer (lower == higher precedence)
- match: object (see match expressions below)
- action: object (route_to / redirect / reject)
- weight: optional list (for split-routing)
- rollout: optional object (canary, stages)
- metadata: optional map (owner, linked-ticket, tags)

Example JSON rule (small, explicit):
{
  "id": "rr-multi-region-translate-2026-01",
  "description": "Route translate models by region, prefer local pool then fallback to us-west pool",
  "priority": 100,
  "match": {
    "models": ["translate-v2", "translate-legacy"],
    "customer_tiers": ["enterprise", "standard"],
    "region_predicate": {"type": "in", "values": ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]},
    "min_tokens": 0,
    "max_tokens": 4096
  },
  "action": {
    "type": "route",
    "primary": {"pool": "eu-local-translate-pool", "model_variant": "quantized-v2"},
    "fallbacks": [
      {"pool": "us-west-translate-pool", "model_variant": "quantized-v2", "reason": "capacity"}
    ]
  },
  "rollout": {
    "canary": {"percentage": 5, "duration_minutes": 30},
    "stages": [
      {"percentage": 5, "duration_minutes": 30},
      {"percentage": 25, "duration_minutes": 60},
      {"percentage": 100, "duration_minutes": 120}
    ],
    "metric_gates": ["p95_latency_ms<2000", "error_rate<0.5%"]
  },
  "metadata": {"owner": "eng-platform-infra", "ticket": "JIRA-PLAT-5210"}
}

YAML variant (recommended for humans):
---
- id: rr-multi-region-translate-2026-01
  description: Route translate models by region
  priority: 100
  match:
    models: [translate-v2, translate-legacy]
    customer_tiers: [enterprise, standard]
    region_predicate:
      type: in
      values: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  action:
    type: route
    primary:
      pool: eu-local-translate-pool
      model_variant: quantized-v2
    fallbacks:
      - pool: us-west-translate-pool
        model_variant: quantized-v2
        reason: capacity
  rollout:
    canary:
      percentage: 5
      duration_minutes: 30
    stages:
      - percentage: 5
        duration_minutes: 30
      - percentage: 25
        duration_minutes: 60
      - percentage: 100
        duration_minutes: 120
    metric_gates: [p95_latency_ms<2000, error_rate<0.5%]

Match expression language (summary):
- Simple key matches: exact or set membership for model names, customer tiers, api_key tags.
- Range checks: token counts, request size, response format length.
- Predicate operators: in, not_in, prefix, suffix, regex, ge, le.
- Composite boolean: and/or/not with explicit parentheses.
- Region semantics: we treat region codes as primary attributes (region, region_group). Region fall-through is explicit (e.g., prefer same-region then region-group then global).

Validation rules (CI / lint):
- Schema conformance: JSON Schema validation for required fields and types.
- Immutable fields: id and created_by are immutable post-apply. Linter flags changes to id.
- Priority uniqueness: no two active rules with identical match predicate and priority; recommend stable priority blocks (100-199 routing, 200-299 fallbacks).
- Weight sums: any split weights must sum to 100% (tolerate floating error within 0.01).
- Fallbacks present: if action.primary references a pool not tagged as global or regional, at least one fallback must be defined.
- Rolling policy present if any stage < 100%: rollout must include metric gates.
- Region validity: region codes must be from the canonical regions list in infra-regions.yaml; linter resolves deprecated region codes.
- Model compatibility: referenced model_variant must exist in model-catalog (link check via API).
- No cyclic fallbacks: fallbacks cannot transitively refer back to the same pool or rule id.

Automated validation harness (CI):
1) syntactic check (yaml/json parse)
2) json-schema validate + custom rule checks (priority, weights)
3) integration lookup: verify pool and model ids via platform APIs in a staging credential context
4) dry-eval: run a simulated request corpus against the new rule and compare routing decisions against expected golden outputs
5) quick-canary smoke: if merged to main, trigger a 1-minute smoke rollout to a non-prod edge with synthetic traces

Unit / system test examples to add to routing-linter repo:
- test_region_preference(): ensure eu request hits eu-local pool when local capacity available.
- test_weighted_split(): 95/5 split actually sends ~5% to alternative variant in 10k synthetic requests (statistical check).
- test_metric_gate_block(): if p95 rises beyond gate, subsequent stage should abort.

Rollout mechanics (recommended automation):
- CI merges config changes to config-repo: a rule change creates a rollout entity with phases.
- Orchestrator applies rollout phases via control-plane API, tagging emitted traces with rollout_id and phase_id.
- Metric evaluator polls (1m cadence) during each stage and evaluates gates (latency, error, throughput, model-quality-ops).
- On pass: advance to next stage. On fail: immediate rollback to previous stable stage and create an incident with auto-snapshot of sampled requests.

Canary formulas and conservative sizing:
- Default canary percentage: max(5%, 100 / active_regions_count) but never > 10% for global-facing changes.
- Ramp schedule: exponential ramp (p_n = min(100, p_prev * 5)) with min durations to collect signal (30—120 minutes depending on request volume).
- Minimum sample size check: require at least 500 routed requests per stage for statistical validity; if not met, extend stage duration.

Observability and tags:
- All routed requests must emit: rule_id, rollout_id (nullable), phase_id (nullable), pool, model_variant, decision_reason.
- Dashboards: per-rule p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, model-qa-regression (if available), cost-per-token.
- Alerts: p95 spike > baseline*2, error_rate > 1% absolute, model_quality_drop > 1% fallover-minute.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- Gate breach (latency/error)
- Elevated 5xx rates or rate-limited responses from pool
- Model hallucination metric (if model-quality signals present)
- Manual abort from on-call

Authoring checklist (pre-PR):
- [ ] id follows rr-<area>-<short-desc>-YYYY-MM (stable pattern)
- [ ] description includes owner, expected impact, and rollback plan
- [ ] match expression is as narrow as possible
- [ ] primary pool and at least one fallback defined
- [ ] rollout defined when change is nontrivial or cross-region
- [ ] linked ticket included in metadata
- [ ] unit tests for dry-eval added

CI/Linter integration tips:
- linter should run as a pre-commit hook and as part of PR gating.
- quickly-fail on invalid region codes to avoid accidental global routing.
- add a warning level for large blast-radius changes (>=50% traffic or cross-region changes to core models).

Operational runbook snippet (for SRE):
- Incident triage: identify rule_id and phase_id in request traces -> check metric gates -> if breach confirmed, call control-plane rollback endpoint with rollout_id -> attach sampled requests and metric snapshots -> postmortem.

Edge-cases, rough notes, and TODOs (notes-to-self):
- We need a standard for model-quality signals and an API to query per-variant QA metrics (currently stubbed).
- Consider adding "time-windowed" match (e.g., only route during peak hours).
- How to represent dependent rulesets (rule A must be evaluated before B even if priority ties) — adding explicit "depends_on" may help but increases complexity.
- Investigate integrating chaos tests that intentionally fail region-local pools during staging to validate fallback correctness.

Appendix: common validation error messages (lint output examples):
- ERROR: rr-id-missing - id missing or empty
- ERROR: invalid-region-code - found region "eu" (expected eu-west-1)
- WARN: wide-match - match expression matches >50% of traffic (blast-radius check)
- ERROR: weight-sum-invalid - split weights sum to 98.7% (expected 100%)
- ERROR: missing-rollout-gates - rollout defined but metric_gates empty

Contact: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — ping on #plat-routing or open PR against config-repo.

Status note: draft but actionable. Plan to merge into config-repo once linter and dry-eval integration complete.
